title: Choose the Updates workspace
question: All three keep the dashboard and Courses design language. Choose the structure that should organize Canvas announcements, assignments, materials, and courses.

options.label: Canvas Briefing
options.lineage: academic morning brief and Refero activity boards
options.thesis: Open on what changed, what needs action, and what can wait.
options.viewport: The shared 32px page header leads into one dark briefing strip for new announcements, open work, and the next deadline; a broad assignment register and narrow announcement pulse begin below it.
options.risk: The briefing must stay quiet when Canvas has little new information.

options.label: Two-Pane Dispatch
options.lineage: Refero inboxes and document review tools
options.thesis: Scan a compact stream on the left and inspect the full Canvas item without losing your place.
options.viewport: Below the shared page header and local tabs, a compact announcement or assignment list occupies the left third while the selected item fills a calm reading pane on the right; filters sit as one edge-to-edge toolbar.
options.risk: It is strongly desktop-native and needs a deliberate drill-in pattern on phones.

options.label: Course Signal Board
options.lineage: course operations register and Refero status tables
options.thesis: Make each current course a signal row, with deadlines, unread news, material coverage, and grade context reconciled in one place.
options.viewport: A broad ruled course register dominates the first viewport; every row exposes its next deadline and Canvas activity while a compact right rail shows the selected course feed and connection health.
options.risk: Chronological urgency across several courses is less immediate than in a true inbox.
